label: VPcmFloModem::v90RunDemodulator.  Run it with: tools/mutate.py --suite v90rundemod
NOTE: the source is shared with the vpcmrunpcm, vpcmflomodem, vpcmep3 and v34diagflo sets.
why: Five sets over one file, one binary each; suites.json maps one name to one source and one binary, and none of the other four drives v90RunDemodulator at all.  Every anchor below is checked unique against the WHOLE file, which includes runPcmModem's near-identical arms -- that is what broke thirteen of vpcmrunpcm's when this function landed (finding 7580).

label: NOTE: THE POLARITY ROW IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.
why: `dispatch 1 case 3 takes runPcmModem's polarity` is finding 7580's first trap written as a mutation: it turns this function into its sibling at the one site where the two differ, and it must come back caught.  The four MP/MPnot rows are the second trap the same way.

why: EQUIVALENT, and the argument is the reason finding 7585 was corrected. `(short)(x * 2)` keeps only the low sixteen bits of `x * 2`, and those depend only on the low sixteen bits of `x` -- so the extension the load uses is discarded and `movswl` against `movzwl` at 0xd5ec is finding 614's free column after all.  The row is kept rather than deleted because the claim it makes is the one 7585 first got wrong.
